title: Fine particles outdoors
description: WHO estimated 4.2 million premature deaths worldwide from outdoor air pollution in 2019; this is a modeled population burden.
keywords: air Fine particles outdoors Fine airborne particles are inhaled from varied sources such as fires, transport, industry and combustion.

title: Polluting household cooking fuels
description: WHO reported about 2.1 billion people worldwide cook using polluting fuels or technologies in its December 2025 fact sheet.
keywords: air Polluting household cooking fuels Burning wood, coal, kerosene or other polluting fuels indoors can create harmful airborne particles.

title: Lead in drinking water
description: WHO states that no level of lead exposure is known to be without harmful effects; young children are especially vulnerable.
keywords: water Lead in drinking water Lead can leach from service lines, solder and plumbing; exposure also occurs through dust, paint and industrial sources.

title: PFAS in water and food
description: NIH reviews associations between exposure to certain PFAS and immune, cholesterol, reproductive and other effects; evidence differs among chemicals.
keywords: water PFAS in water and food Some PFAS can reach people through drinking water, food and occupational or product-related routes.

title: Arsenic in groundwater
description: WHO identifies long-term inorganic arsenic exposure through drinking water as a cause of cancer and other harmful outcomes.
keywords: water Arsenic in groundwater Natural geology can introduce arsenic into aquifers used for drinking, cooking and irrigation.

title: Methylmercury in fish
description: WHO identifies methylmercury as a concern for fetal and early-childhood neurological development; some fish accumulate more than others.
keywords: food-waste Methylmercury in fish Mercury can transform in aquatic ecosystems, build up in fish and reach people through seafood.

title: Electronic waste and unsafe recycling
description: WHO reports 62 million tonnes of e-waste generated globally in 2022; just 22.3% was documented as formally collected and recycled.
keywords: food-waste Electronic waste and unsafe recycling Unsafe burning, dismantling and dumping can expose workers and communities to hazardous air, dust, soil and water mixtures.

title: Radon inside buildings
description: U.S. EPA identifies radon as a naturally occurring radioactive gas that can cause lung cancer; it cannot be seen or smelled.
keywords: home-work Radon inside buildings Radon can enter buildings from soil and accumulate indoors; actual concentration differs by building.

title: Heat and preventable illness
description: CDC describes heat exhaustion, heat stroke and other heat-related illness risks, with greater danger in certain health and working conditions.
keywords: home-work Heat and preventable illness Indoor or outdoor heat, physical activity and barriers to cooling can overwhelm the body's temperature control.

title: Respirable silica at work
description: CDC/NIOSH warns that breathing respirable crystalline silica during certain jobs can lead to silicosis and other serious diseases.
keywords: home-work Respirable silica at work Cutting, drilling, grinding and polishing some stone and other materials can produce fine respirable silica dust.

title: WHO ambient air quality database
description: Annual average PM2.5, PM10 and nitrogen dioxide concentrations for selected settlements. A historical city-wide annual mean is not today's local AQI or a personal exposure measurement.
keywords: World Health Organization City and town measurements from 127 WHO members, associate members or territories; not every settlement. June 2026 version, observations from 2010–2024

title: AirNow air-quality information
description: AQI levels, smoke information and health-oriented air-quality categories. A monitor or sensor does not identify all local exposures, individual doses or a responsible facility.
keywords: U.S. EPA and partner agencies U.S. location-level monitors and forecasts; availability varies by place and pollutant. Current/forecast AQI with real-time data caveats

title: EPA ECHO facility compliance
description: Facility permit details, inspection records, reported violations and enforcement actions. A listed violation can be alleged rather than finally adjudicated; missing records do not prove a facility is safe.
keywords: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency Facilities recorded in applicable EPA and state/tribal environmental reporting systems. Mixed enforcement, permit and reporting windows

title: EPA Toxics Release Inventory
description: Reported chemical releases, waste transfers and pollution-prevention information. Pounds released are not a measured population dose or toxicity ranking, and some tools may be offline.
keywords: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency Facilities and chemicals meeting TRI reporting rules, not every source of pollution. Annual self-reported releases; the EPA toolbox lists current tool status

title: Annual drinking-water quality reports
description: Water sources, reported regulated contaminants, violations and supplier contacts. A supplier-wide report cannot substitute for a qualified lead or other contaminant test at one tap.
keywords: U.S. EPA and local public water systems Community public-water suppliers; not a private well or a household's individual tap. Annual reports from water suppliers

title: European Air Quality Index
description: Short-term air quality estimates for PM2.5, PM10, NO2, ozone and SO2. The Index is not a legal compliance determination or a long-term annual air-quality assessment.
keywords: European Environment Agency European monitoring stations and modeled air-quality areas; data availability varies. Near-real-time station information and model forecasts

title: European Industrial Emissions Portal
description: Reported industrial releases to air, water and land, transfers of waste and facility details. An annual reported mass does not show local exposure or prove legal responsibility.
keywords: European Environment Agency Major industrial complexes under covered European reporting requirements, not all businesses. Annual facility and pollutant reports; check reporting year

title: Canadian Air Quality Health Index
description: A health-oriented indicator based on air pollutant measurements and forecast conditions. A community AQHI is not an individual exposure estimate and local conditions can vary.
keywords: Environment and Climate Change Canada Canadian AQHI reporting communities; station and location coverage varies. Current conditions and forecasts

title: National Pollutant Release Inventory
description: Facility-reported air, water, and land releases, disposals and transfers. Preliminary data can contain reporting errors; facility releases are not individual dose measurements.
keywords: Government of Canada Reporting facilities and substances under NPRI thresholds across Canada. 2025 records are labeled preliminary in the current search tool

title: Check air quality in the UK
description: Air quality by locality or postcode, alerts and exposure guidance. A local forecast is an indicator, not a personal diagnosis or source-attribution model.
keywords: UK Department for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs Area-level air forecasts and available monitors in the UK. Current monitoring and forecasts where provided

title: Environment Agency Pollution Inventory
description: Reported annual releases to air and water and waste movements from qualifying sites. Large sites are covered selectively; reported annual masses do not describe personal exposure.
keywords: Environment Agency / UK National Data Library Regulated major industrial sites in England within the inventory's reporting scope. Downloadable annual data for 2013–2024 at the time of review

title: Australian National Pollutant Inventory
description: Annual releases and waste transfers of listed NPI pollutants, including facility mapping. Different chemicals cannot be summed into a meaningful total-harm ranking; reported release is not confirmed exposure.
keywords: Australian Government DCCEEW Australian facilities and diffuse sources within NPI reporting rules. 2024–25 reporting period, updates/corrections possible
